centre.how: The Romanos dye-works, the largest excavation, at its published coordinates 38 deg 13.330' N, 22 deg 7.895' E (Table I); within 25 m of the first Wikidata point and the OpenStreetMap 'early Hellenistic settlement' node. Wikidata holds a second point 1.1 km east.

claimed.line: Helike, a Greek city by the sea, sank in a night in 373 BCE; the Helike Project and the BBC call it the likely seed of Atlantis.
claimed.who: Dora Katsonopoulou and Steven Soter (Helike Project); BBC Horizon
claimed.evidence: Its destruction was one of the most appalling tragedies of the classical world and most probably the reality behind the myth of Atlantis.

found.line: Sonar at sea found no city. Classical walls lie 3 m down in lagoon mud 1 km inland; whether they are the 373 BCE city is open.
found.evidence: A Classical site 130m away, buried under 3m of similar sediments, may have been destroyed by the earthquake and tsunami of 373 B.C.

features.label: Edgerton sonar target, 42 m deep
features.what: A sonar target below the sea floor, under 42 m of water off the Selinous mouth, that Edgerton's team thought might be ruins.
features.result: Three boreholes drilled in 1973 to test it were inconclusive; the 1988 sonar survey found no clear city on or under the sea floor.

position.detail: Text, page 541: 'about 1400 m north of the Selinous River mouth' (the introduction says 'northeast of the Selinous River mouth'). Point placed 1400 m due north of the mouth of the Selinous (OpenStreetMap way 801939054, end node).

features.evidence: which lay under water 42 m deep, about 1400 m north of the Selinous River mouth
features.notes: Edgerton's own reports (1973, 1979, 1981) were not fetched. The two descriptions in one paper differ: 'northeast of' (page 532) and 'about 1400 m north of' (page 541). Wikipedia dates the Edgerton and Throckmorton search to 1967; the 1999 paper says 1966 to 1974.

features.label: 1988 sonar survey, 8 km2 of sea floor
features.who: Helike Project (Soter, Katsonopoulou, with Kron and others)
features.what: Sidescan and subbottom sonar survey of about 8 km2 of sea floor off the delta, northwest of the Vouraikos mouth, to test whether Helike lay under the sea.
features.result: Showed geological signs of earthquakes but no clear city on or under the sea floor, apart from one structure that resembles an ancient mole at Elaion; the search moved onto land.

position.detail: Figure 1 (page 532), a 1:50,000 map with two grid ticks (22 deg 10' E at the top, 38 deg 15' N at the right edge) and a 4 km bar. Scale 114.75 px per km (bar). The map prints the offshore boundary only, as a line running from the shore near Digeliotika to the Vouraikos delta. I closed the landward side along the present OpenStreetMap shoreline, which the paper does not draw. Closed polygon area 8.8 km2 against the paper's 8 km2. Check: the Klonis site read off the same figure falls 116 m from its published coordinates.

features.evidence: in 1988 the Helike Project carried out a systematic sidescan and subbottom sonar survey of 8 km2 of the seafloor
features.notes: The inshore edge is the 2026 coast, not drawn by the authors; the true inshore limit of the 1988 survey is not published in the papers I read. The first report (Soter and Katsonopoulou 1998a) was not fetched.

features.label: 1973 offshore holes at the target (x3)
features.who: IOKAE (now the National Centre for Marine Research), reported by Schwartz and Tziavos
features.what: Three offshore boreholes drilled to test Edgerton's sonar target in 42 m of water.
features.result: Cores held marine silt with shells and coral over sand and gravel; the results were inconclusive and showed no city.

position.detail: Same point as the Edgerton target (page 541: the holes were drilled to investigate it). The three hole positions are not published in the papers I read.

column.what: upper layer: clayey marine silt with shells and coral
lower layer: clayey marine silt with shells and coral

features.evidence: The offshore cores sampled two layers of clayey marine silt (with shells and coral) alternating with layers of sand and gravel
features.notes: Depths are those on page 541: the upper silt about 3 m below the sea floor, the lower silt 5 to 9 m. The silts alternate with sand and gravel, so the column lists only the dated silts. Original report: Schwartz and Tziavos 1979 (not fetched).

features.label: S4: 50 m hole on the beach (1973)
features.who: IOKAE, reported by Schwartz and Tziavos
features.what: A 50 m borehole on the beach just north of the Selinous mouth.
features.result: Sand and gravel to 12 m, then silt or clay alternating with gravel and sand; no ancient remains reported.

position.detail: Figure 3, symbol S4. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

column.what: layers of silt or clay alternating with sand and gravel

features.evidence: The top 12 m was sand and gravel, and the rest consisted of layers of silt or clay alternating with clastics
features.notes: Described in the 1999 paper (page 541); the symbol position is read from the 2011 paper's Figure 3.

features.label: G1 and G2: 1983 geotechnical holes
features.what: Boreholes near the shore west of the Kerynites mouth, drilled to study how the ground would fail in an earthquake.
features.result: Same layering as S4: gravel and sand at the top, then soft clay and silt; the authors suggested liquefaction or sliding along clay seams could have sunk Helike.

position.detail: Figure 3, symbol 'G1,2' (two holes drawn as one symbol). Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: Leonards et al. suggested that the subsidence of ancient Helike was caused either by soil liquefaction or mass sliding along inclined clay seams
features.notes: Original: Leonards et al. 1988 (not fetched). Two holes share one symbol, so one point is given.

features.label: G3: 1983 geotechnical hole
features.what: A third geotechnical borehole near the shore west of the Kerynites mouth.
features.result: Stratigraphy very similar to S4 and G1-G2.

position.detail: Figure 3, symbol G3. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: The stratigraphy was very similar to that of S4, with clastics dominant in the top 10 m

features.result: Hit an overpressured water-bearing sand and gravel layer at 11 to 14 m, which forced sand up the drill stem.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B1. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.label: B5: deep midplain hole
features.what: One of the first five boreholes, drilled more than 40 m deep in the midplain.
features.result: Hit an overpressured aquifer at 16 to 21 m.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B5. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: Bore holes B1, B5, and B4 (listed here from north to south) were all located in the midplain at surface elevations of 8–9 m above MSL
features.notes: As B1.

features.label: B4: 38 m hole, marine mud at depth
features.what: Deep midplain borehole, 38.5 m sampled.
features.result: Marine sediment at 38.5 m, about 8,400 years old, shows the sea reached this site before the delta filled in.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B4. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.label: B14: abraded microfossils at 11.6 m
features.what: Borehole in the northwest of the delta where microfossils at 11.6 m are broken and mixed from several environments.
features.result: Mixed, abraded microfossils may reflect tsunami deposition, but the authors call the reading hypothetical.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B14. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: We found such assemblages in borehole B14 at 11.6m depth, in B16 at 7.7m
features.notes: The asterisk beside 14 in Figure 3 marks 'possible tsunami deposit'. The authors stress that storm surge or earthquake sand blows could give the same signal.

features.label: B16: abraded microfossils at 7.7 m
features.what: Borehole close to the Classical site with broken, mixed microfossils at 7.7 m.
features.result: A possible, not proven, tsunami signal.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B16. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: We found such assemblages in borehole B14 at 11.6m depth, in B16 at 7.7m
features.notes: See B14.

features.label: B58: dated cores to 13.65 m
features.what: Borehole with two dated samples and abraded, mixed microfossils at 2.65 m and 12 m.
features.result: Carbon and charcoal at 8.25 m and 13.65 m date to about 6,400 and 5,800 years ago; the mixed microfossils are a possible tsunami signal.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B58. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.label: B61: marine fibres at 17.55 m
features.what: Borehole with dated wood at 10.4 m and sea-grass fibres at 17.55 m.
features.result: Sea-grass fibres at 17.55 m are marine and about 5,800 years old; wood at 10.4 m is about 6,250 years old.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B61. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.label: B72: dated cores to 13.9 m
features.what: Borehole on the higher ground west of the main site with two dated carbon samples.
features.result: Carbon at 10.2 m is about 3,100 years old and at 13.9 m about 6,600 years old.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B72. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.notes: The deeper date has a large error (430 years).

features.label: B84: 22 m, did not reach the gravel
features.what: Borehole in the deepest part of the basin, drilled to 22 m below a surface 9 m above sea level.
features.result: Did not reach the first coarse gravel layer (horizon C), so the fine lagoon mud there is more than 22 m thick.

position.detail: Figure 3, borehole B84. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: 9m, but did not penetrate horizon C
features.notes: Labelled 84 in Figure 6.

features.label: B91: occupation horizons at 3.6 to 5.7 m
features.what: Borehole 50 m northeast of trench H21 in the Early Bronze Age (Saitis) area.
features.result: Three occupation horizons at 3.6, 4.4 and 5.7 m depth.

position.detail: Table I gives B91 as '50m NE of H21'; H21 is 38 deg 13.037' N, 22 deg 8.190' E. Point offset 50 m at 45 degrees.

features.evidence: Occupation horizons at 3.6, 4.4, and 5.7m.
features.notes: Offset from a published coordinate. The year is the drilling campaign around B73 and B75; it is not stated for B91.

features.label: B73 and trench H1: Hellenistic wall
features.what: Georadar target at 2.4 m, drilled as borehole B73 in 1998 and opened as trench H1 in 2000 on the same spot.
features.result: A well-built Hellenistic wall at about 2.4 m, and below it at 3.85 m a layer of fine sand with abraded microfossils that may be tsunami deposit, or a storm surge.

position.detail: Table I, Romanos site: B73 at 38 deg 13.348' N, 22 deg 7.863' E; the only trench coinciding with a borehole.

column.what: fine floodplain sediments (Roman road at 1.65 m in neighbouring trench H12)
fine stratified sand with abraded brackish and marine ostracods and foraminifera
column.age: possibly the 373 BCE tsunami; storm surge not excluded

features.evidence: Trench H1 revealed a well-built wall at ca. 2.4 m depth, dated to the Hellenistic period (3rd/2nd century B.C.) based on associated finds.
features.notes: The text lists ceramic horizons in B73 at 2.1, 2.9 and 4.7 m; Table I lists 2.1 and 2.65 to 3.15 m. Table I puts the H1 wall at 2.5 m, the text at 2.4 m.

features.label: Hellenistic dye-works (Romanos)
features.what: A major textile dye-works, about 39 by 25 m (about 975 m2), with four pebble-floored cisterns, vats, rooms, storage and workshops about 2.3 m down; the largest excavation at Helike.
features.result: Early to Middle Hellenistic pottery and coins date it to after the 373 BCE earthquake, so it belongs to the town rebuilt there, not the destroyed Classical city.

position.detail: Table I, Romanos: 'Rectangular area 39 x 25 m centered at ~38 deg 13.330' N, 22 deg 7.895' E'. The rectangle's orientation is not published, so a point is given. OpenStreetMap node 9160301491 ('early Hellenistic settlement') lies 25 m away and the first Wikidata coordinate 23 m.

features.evidence: complex of four pebbled floor cisterns with surrounding vats and other structures for washing and dyeing fabrics
features.notes: The 2011 paper gives no year for the dye-works trenches ('a series of trenches about 50 m southeast of H12'), so none is given here. The 2024 Geosciences abstract says a strong earthquake destroyed the dye-works.

features.label: Klonis: Roman building (1995)
features.what: Two 4 m squares opened over a magnetic anomaly found by the 1994 magnetometer survey.
features.result: A large Late Roman building with standing walls 1.5 to 3.6 m high, destroyed by an earthquake probably in the late 5th century CE; Classical, Geometric and Mycenaean sherds lay deeper but not in place.

position.detail: Table I, Klonis (KL): 38 deg 13.030' N, 22 deg 7.942' E.

features.evidence: Excavation revealed a large Roman building with walls standing 2 m high constructed with successive layers of unworked stone, baked bricks, and mortar as binding material.
features.notes: The BBC page describes this Roman building as one of the false starts.

features.label: Papafilippou: tile layer, 330-300 BCE
features.what: Trench H9 and three neighbours (H11, H29, H35), opened from 2000.
features.result: A thick layer of roof tiles, pottery and coins about 2 m down, dated to about 330 to 300 BCE, after the 373 BCE earthquake; under it a well-built stone wall at 2.1 m.

position.detail: Table I, Papafilippou (PF), trench H9: 38 deg 13.210' N, 22 deg 7.807' E. H11, H29 and H35 are 'same area'.

column.what: destruction layer of roof tiles, pottery, loom weights and bronze coins
well-built stone wall (trench H29, under the destruction layer)

features.evidence: All trenches revealed a thick destruction layer at about 2.0m depth, containing a large number of plain and painted roof tiles and potsherds

features.label: Papamichalopoulou: Late Classical graves
features.what: Two trenches (2002, 2003) about 200 m northwest of Papafilippou.
features.result: Seven tile-covered graves of the late 4th to early 3rd century BCE at 1.9 m, under a Roman destruction layer at 1.1 m.

position.detail: Table I, Papamichalopoulou (PM), trenches H25 and H33: 38 deg 13.250' N, 22 deg 7.687' E.

features.evidence: tile-covered graves of the late 4th to early 3rd centuries B.C.

features.label: Balalas H18: Classical walls, 3.2 m
features.what: Trench H18, opened 2001 in the Balalas field about 130 m northwest of the Early Bronze Age area.
features.result: The Roman road at 2.3 m, a Hellenistic wall at 2.9 m and a Classical wall at 3.15 to 3.4 m.

position.detail: Table I, Balalas (BL), trench H18: 38 deg 13.095' N, 22 deg 8.129' E.

features.evidence: revealed the Roman road at 2.3m depth, and the remains of walls at 2.9 and 3.15–3.4m, dated on the basis of associated pottery to Hellenistic and Classical times, respectively
features.notes: Table I gives 'about 3.0 and 3.4 m' for the two walls; the text gives 2.9 and 3.15 to 3.4 m.

features.label: H19: Classical building corner, 3 m down
features.what: Trench H19, 24 m south of H18 in the same field, opened 2001.
features.result: The corner of a Classical building 3 m down, below the water table; wall stones thrown seaward and worn pottery, a pattern the authors say fits tsunami backwash.

position.detail: Table I: H19 is '24m S of H18'; H18 is 38 deg 13.095' N, 22 deg 8.129' E. Point offset 24 m south.

column.what: corner walls of a Classical building with pottery, a bronze coin of Aigina and a silver coin of Sikyon
column.age: Classical; Aigina coin early 4th century, Sikyon coin about 340 to 330 BCE

features.evidence: Trench H19 revealed the corner of a Classical building 3 m below the surface (Figure 9). Only the corner of the building remains in situ; everything else was apparently swept away.
features.notes: The authors write that 'evidence based on stratigraphy and archaeological excavation is merely suggestive' of the 373 BCE event. The Sikyon coin is dated about 340 to 330 BCE, after 373 BCE, which the paper does not discuss. Stiros (2020) argues that part of the site was reoccupied within 40 years.

features.label: Saitis: Bronze Age town, 3.3 m down
features.what: Eight trenches (H7, H21, H22, H26, H38, H43, H51, H61) opened from 2000 to 2007 on the site found by borehole B75.
features.result: Well-preserved stone buildings, cobbled streets and intact pottery of about 2500 to 2200 BCE, with signs of fire, under 3 to 5 m of lagoon mud; 130 m from the Classical site.

position.detail: Table I, Saitis (ST), trench H21: 38 deg 13.037' N, 22 deg 8.190' E. The other trenches are shown only in the plan in Figure 10, which has no coordinates, so only H21 and the offsets B75, B91 and H22 are placed.

column.what: Early Helladic III buildings and complete pottery

features.evidence: We discovered a well-preserved EBA settlement about 1 km inland from the present shore, buried under 3 to 5 m of fine sediments containing marine, brackish, and freshwater microfossils.
features.notes: The authors say the settlement may sit on a tell about 3 m high on the seaward shore of a lagoon, and was abandoned about 2200 or 2150 BCE. They found no evidence of a tsunami for that event.

features.label: H22: cobbled street, gold and silver
features.what: Trench H22, 23 m north of H21.
features.result: Early Bronze Age cobbled street, rectangular and apsidal buildings, a rare depas cup and items in gold and silver; a long wall shifted sideways by about 25 cm.

position.detail: Table I: H22 is '23m N of H21'; H21 is 38 deg 13.037' N, 22 deg 8.190' E.

features.evidence: A long wall in H22 is broken by a right lateral offset of about 25cm
features.notes: The authors cannot say whether the 25 cm offset happened when the site drowned or much later. The paper gives no year for this trench.

features.label: B75: burned layer, 4400 years old
features.what: Borehole drilled in 1998, 17 m east of the later trench H21, to 11 m.
features.result: Pottery from 3 m down, then a rich burned layer of pottery, bone and charcoal at 5.2 to 6.6 m; charcoal at 6.4 m dated to about 4400 years ago, Early Bronze Age.

position.detail: Table I: B75 is '17 m E of H21'; H21 is 38 deg 13.037' N, 22 deg 8.190' E. Point offset 17 m east.

column.age: charcoal at 6.4 m: 4400 +/- 120 years before 1950, calibrated (Table II, Beta 125829)

features.evidence: Charcoal at 6.4m gave a calibrated radiocarbon age of 4400
features.notes: Table I lists horizons at 2.0, 3.0, 5.2 to 6.6 and 7.5 m; the text says 3.0 to 6.6 m. The Table II age is 4400 +/- 120, calibrated.

features.label: Komnenos: Roman store, skeleton
features.what: Trenches H13, H14 and H16 opened in 2001 over a georadar target under a local road.
features.result: Large Roman buildings and a store with a 2 m deep tank; a human skeleton lay crushed under fallen debris on the steps, a possible sign of a Roman-period earthquake.

position.detail: Table I, Komnenos (KM), trench H14: 38 deg 12.677' N, 22 deg 8.377' E.

features.evidence: A human skeleton was found crushed under fallen debris on the steps descending into the tank, possible evidence of an earthquake in Roman times.

features.label: Karelis: five Roman tile graves
features.what: Trench H5 opened in 2000 in a vineyard over a strong georadar anomaly.
features.result: Five tile-covered graves of the 2nd to 3rd century CE about 1.5 m down; the roof tiles caused the radar reflections.

position.detail: Table I, Karelis (KR), trench H5: 38 deg 12.620' N, 22 deg 8.470' E.

features.evidence: Excavation revealed a group of five tile-covered tombs containing grave goods dated to the 2nd to 3rd centuries AD

features.label: Nikolaiika: Geometric, Mycenaean
features.what: Trench H58 near the Kerynites River in Nikolaiika (2006), then H59 (2007).
features.result: Seven Roman tile-covered tombs at 1.3 to 2.0 m, with Geometric pottery at 2.1 to 2.3 m and Mycenaean pottery at 3.8 to 4.1 m.

position.detail: Table I, Dimopoulou (DM), trench H58: 38 deg 12.543' N, 22 deg 8.571' E.

features.evidence: Excavation of deeper archaeological horizons revealed fine pottery of the Geometric and Mycenaean periods, at 2.1–2.3 and 3.8–4.1m, respectively.
features.notes: An OpenStreetMap node labelled 'Geometric temple of Nikolaiika' (node 11972271725) lies about 110 m south-southwest of H58; it cites no paper and I left it out.

features.label: Roman road, traced 800 m in 9 trenches
features.what: A straight Roman road 5 to 6 m wide, 0.7 m thick, built of cobbles, gravel and packed soil, crossing the Romanos, Balalas and Saitis sites.
features.result: Excavated in nine trenches over a straight course of 800 m; it lies about 1.65 m down at Romanos and 1.8 to 2.3 m down at Balalas and Saitis.

position.detail: Line through four published trench positions on the road: H3 (45 m NW of B73), B73/H1, H18 and H21 (Table I). The paper says the course is straight and 800 m long; the four points are collinear to within 20 m and the line is 0.79 km long.

features.evidence: The road was excavated in nine trenches, which allowed us to trace its straight course for 800 m
features.notes: Built in the Augustan period, centuries after 373 BCE; it fixes the line of the excavated strip.

features.label: Roman road, 1.3 km (tomography)
features.what: Electrical resistivity tomography detected the road and extended its known length to 1300 m.
features.result: The straight line drawn in Figure 3 runs from Romanos southeast to borehole 92.

position.detail: Figure 3: the black line. North end taken at the published B73/H1 position (the line starts at the RM symbol), south end read at the centre of borehole symbol 92. Figure 3 (page 588), a 1:5000-based map with no printed grid; fitted by least squares to the nine Table I trench coordinates (RM, PM, PF, KL, BL, ST, KM, KR, DM; residuals 8 to 44 m, rms about 27 m); borehole symbol centre read by eye, about 3 m per pixel

features.evidence: Tsokas et al. (2009) detected the road with electrical tomography and extended its known length to 1300m
features.notes: The line as drawn measures about 1.2 km, a little short of 1300 m. Tsokas and others 2009 itself was not fetched.

features.label: Ancient lagoon basin (modelled)
features.what: Dotted contour enclosing where the top of the first coarse gravel (horizon C) lies below today's sea level, which the authors read as the site of an ancient lagoon behind a beach barrier.
features.result: The buried Classical and Early Bronze Age sites sit at the lagoon margin; the lagoon is a model drawn from borehole depths, not a mapped shoreline.

position.detail: Figure 6 (page 597), the dotted contour. Figure 6 has the same base map and scale as Figure 3 but is shifted by (+17, +180) px, found by cross-correlating the two maps' line-work (match score 3.7 times the next best). Then as for Figure 3. The loop was traced by hand along the printed dots; error widened for the thin dotted line.

features.evidence: The dotted contour in Figure 6 encloses the area where horizon C lies below nominal sea level, which suggests the location of an ancient lagoon, bounded by a barrier beach.
features.notes: Defined against the 1:5000 military map's 1966 'nominal' elevations; recent surveys find ground west of the Kerynites up to 2.5 m lower than that map. Enclosed area as digitised: about 1.1 km2; the paper gives no figure.

features.label: Black clay layer (Byzantine marsh)
features.what: Shaded zone in Figure 6 where a 20 to 40 cm layer of black clay lies 1 to 3 m below ground.
features.result: Freshwater microfossils only; it lies over the Roman road, so a shallow marsh covered the Classical and Early Bronze Age sites in Byzantine times.

position.detail: Figure 6, grey fill 'Dark Clay'. Same transform as the lagoon outline. Outline taken from the shaded fill and smoothed to a convex shape. My polygon is about 0.87 km2; the paper's text gives about 0.7 km2.

features.evidence: we found a shallow layer of black clay, about 0.7km2 in area, shown by the shaded region in Figure 6
features.notes: The digitised area is about 20 per cent larger than the number in the text; I kept the figure's shape and note the gap.

features.label: Present shoreline
features.what: Today's coast of the Gulf of Corinth between Aigio and the Vouraikos mouth.
features.result: The excavated Classical and Early Bronze Age sites are 1.0 to 1.7 km inland of it; the authors say no occupation horizons were found within 800 m of the shore.

position.detail: OpenStreetMap natural=coastline ways, joined and simplified to 25 m, clipped to 8 km of the site centre. Fetched 2026-11-11 with the Overpass API.

features.evidence: natural=coastline
features.notes: The coast has moved seaward since antiquity by sediment and uplift: 'A house built on the shore between the Selinous and Kerynites Rivers in the 1890s is now about 350 m from the sea' (Soter and Katsonopoulou 1999). Joined from several OSM ways; the id shown is one of them.

story.line: Ancient writers say a city called Helike, 12 stades from the sea, sank in a winter night in 373 BCE; Pausanias saw drowned ruins.
From 1966 Harold Edgerton's sonar found a target under 42 m of water; three holes drilled in 1973 settled nothing.
In 1988 the Helike Project swept 8 km2 of sea floor with sonar and saw no clear city, so it moved onto land.
On land, 99 boreholes from 1991 found pottery under about 2 km2 of delta between the Selinous and Kerynites rivers.
Digging from 2000 found a Classical building corner 3 m down at Balalas, an Early Bronze Age town 130 m away, and a Roman road.
The finds lie in old lagoon mud now above sea level: the city was buried, then lifted, not found under the sea.
The link to Atlantis stays a proposal: the 373 BCE tsunami layer is only suggestive, and Stiros argues for inland mudflows.

not_verified: Marinatos 1960, Edgerton 1973, 1979 and 1981, Schwartz and Tziavos 1979, Leonards and others 1988, Soter and Katsonopoulou 1998a: cited as the 1999 and 2011 papers describe them; none fetched.
Alvarez-Zarikian, Soter and Katsonopoulou 2008 (microfossils): Crossref gave the title only and the open copy on journals.flvc.org returned 403; the lagoon reading is taken from the 2011 paper.
MDPI papers (Land 2025, Geosciences 2024) returned 403 to scripted requests; I read their Crossref abstracts only. The 'about every 300 years' number is from that abstract.
Stiros 2020 (The Holocene) and the 2022 Seismological Research Letters comment and reply: Crossref abstracts only; Stiros's 2022 original paper was not located.
helikeproject.gr home page is a frame set; the pages inside were not read.
Aelian, On Animals 11.19 and Ovid: quoted only as the 1999 and 2011 papers quote them (the papers cite Aelian as 11.9 and 11.19); our library holds only Aelian's Various History 3.18.
Plato's dates and the c. 360 BCE date of the Timaeus come from Wikipedia; no scholarly source was fetched for the Timaeus date.
The datum of the Table I coordinates is not stated; they agree with Wikidata and OpenStreetMap to about 25 m, so I treat them as WGS84.

Excavations after 2008 (the Late Classical to Hellenistic settlement in the western plain, the 2012 destruction layer) are named by Wikipedia and the Geosciences abstract, but their positions are not published in anything I could open.
